definitions.explanation: A mimetic word ({擬態語|ぎたいご}) for something so soft that it has no stiffness of its own and bends or collapses under the slightest force — melted plastic, an overcooked noodle, a sleeping child's arm.

examples.japanese: {体|からだ}がくにゃくにゃになった。
{熱|ねつ}でスプーンがくにゃくにゃに{曲|ま}がった。
examples.english: The spoon bent limply in the heat.

examples.japanese: この{人形|にんぎょう}は{中|なか}に{針金|はりがね}が{入|はい}っていないので、くにゃくにゃして{立|た}たない。
examples.english: This doll has no wire inside, so it is too floppy to stand up.

notes:
Used both of physical objects that lack rigidity and of a body with no strength in it. Common as くにゃくにゃになる (to go limp) and as a な-form modifier, くにゃくにゃな.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- くにゃくにゃになる: to go limp, to lose all stiffness
- くにゃくにゃ{曲|ま}がる: to bend floppily
- くにゃくにゃした{素材|そざい}: a floppy material

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ぐにゃぐにゃ: limp, misshapen — the voiced form; heavier and more deformed
- ふにゃふにゃ: soft and limp — emphasizes softness to the touch rather than bending
- やわらかい: soft — the neutral adjective, with no image of collapsing
